gate.h: From Space to a Greener Kuwait
gate.p: This opening has sound: a launch countdown and an original, fully synthesised rocket sound design. Your browser will only play it if you ask for it here.
gate.n: You can switch the sound on or off at any point during the sequence.
intro.title: From Space to a Greener Kuwait
hero.lede: KuwaitSat-1 looks down. This platform is the layer that turns what a satellite sees into something a planner can act on — an operational pipeline from imagery, to environmental analysis, to a greening recommendation.
fact.note: Verified specifications from the KuwaitSat-1 project team's published mission paper and Kuwait University releases. Sources are listed at the foot of this page.
leg.h: Every panel declares what it is
leg.lede: A platform that mixes measurement with modelling has one obligation: never let a viewer confuse the two. Every chart, map and image on this site carries one of these four badges.
leg.p1: Published, attributable fact or imagery from KuwaitSat-1 and its project team. Source always linked.
leg.p5: Official open statistics — World Bank, WMO, Kuwaiti government publications. Figure, year and publisher shown.
leg.p4: Reference dataset, modelled on published Kuwaiti environmental patterns and used consistently across every panel.
leg.p2: Values produced by the platform's environmental model. Physically consistent, derived rather than measured.
leg.p3: Interpretation generated by the rule-based analyst in this page. Decision support, never a decision.
leg.unv: Where a detail could not be confirmed against a reliable source, this platform says so in place of the detail: “Information not independently verified.”
leg.warn: Nothing on this site is an official planning proposal or a government recommendation, and no panel carries live satellite telemetry. This is an environmental intelligence platform built on the KuwaitSat-1 mission record.
mis.lede: Kuwait's first national satellite is a 2U CubeSat built by a Kuwait University team. Everything in this table is published by the project or its partners — this platform is built on top of it, and never on top of claims the spacecraft has not made.
mis.note: The satellite's stated primary objective was capacity building and testing whether the camera can support attitude determination — not operational environmental monitoring. This platform proposes the analytical layer that such a mission could feed.
mis.gsp: Kuwait University's College of Science ground station became operational in October 2022: a UHF antenna for telemetry, tracking and command, and an S-band antenna for image downlink, both on rotator controllers.
blt.eyebrow: From the satellite, back to the people
blt.lede: Every frame in this platform starts with a spacecraft that a group of Kuwaitis designed, integrated, tested and now operates from a campus in Kuwait City. Kuwait's first national satellite was built by Kuwait University students and staff, led by project director Dr Hala Al-Jassar, with support from the Kuwait Foundation for the Advancement of Sciences, CITRA and partners.
blt.note: The official project site names its leadership, its control team and its members individually. The numbers reported by Kuwaiti press around the launch — a cohort selected from a much larger pool of applicants, working from 2019 — are attributed to those reports rather than restated here as our own finding.
img.lede: On 5 April 2023, KuwaitSat-1 returned its first series of images of Kuwait — five consecutive frames, each about 80 km across, stitched by the project team into a mosaic of the country's eastern half.
img.disc: The photographs themselves are the property of the KuwaitSat-1 project and Kuwait University. They are not copied into this platform. Each frame below records the real acquisition — footprint, date, resolution and credit — and links to the publisher so the original can be viewed at source.
img.mosp: Where the five frames fell, drawn to the published 80 km swath over a simplified national outline. The footprint is real; the outline is a schematic drawing, not a survey product.
exp.lede: A working Earth-observation viewer: pan, zoom, switch analytical layers, and step back through time. The base scene is generated by this page at a 39 m sampling grid — the KuwaitSat-1 ground sample distance — so the interface behaves like the real thing without ever passing a synthetic frame off as a real one.
dash.lede: The national picture at a glance, for the selected area and period. Figures come from the platform's reference dataset, modelled on published Kuwaiti climate and land-cover patterns.
dash.note: Reference dataset. Operational figures are drawn from calibrated satellite products, ground stations and field survey once those feeds are connected.
map.lede: Kuwait's six governorates, scored by the KuwaitSat-1 greening model. Select a region to see what the model looked at and why it scored the way it did. A high score is an invitation to investigate — not an instruction to plant.
map.recp: What the system says about the selected area — written the way a screening tool should write, with its evidence, its options, its uncertainty and its follow-up all on the same card.
sys.lede: The question is not “where should we plant trees”. It is how Kuwait can use satellite technology, environmental data and AI to make its cities cooler, greener and more resilient to extreme heat. Greening is one instrument in that system — not the whole of it.
sys.cyclep: A one-off recommendation is a guess that never learns. The value is the loop: every intervention becomes the baseline the next pass is measured against.
sys.cyclen: The platform does not simply say where to plant. It turns environmental data into a continuing cycle of analysis, planning, visualisation and monitoring — with a person deciding at every gate.
sys.inp: What the model actually looks at
sys.inpp: Each input is labelled with what kind of data it is. Every figure names its origin. No panel presents a feed this platform does not carry.
sim.lede: Pick an area, run the greening engine, then drag the handle. The left half is the current modelled surface; the right half is the scenario the engine proposes. Both are renderings — the point is the shape of the change, not the pixels.
sim.warn: Modelled scenario — not an official planning proposal. Species, siting, water demand and cost all require field study before any of this becomes a plan.
calc.lede: Move the inputs and watch the modelled indicators respond. Every number here is arithmetic on assumptions you can see — open the assumptions panel to read them.
calc.warn: Modelled estimate. Realised environmental benefit depends on species, irrigation, soil, survival rate and maintenance, and must be established by field measurement and validated models — not by this calculator.
viz.lede: Filter the reference dataset by area, period and metric. Every view is drawn from the same numbers, so the charts and the table always agree.
cmp.lede: Put two epochs side by side, then wipe between them. The change-detection readout is produced by differencing the two rendered scenes — the method is real, the scenes are simulated.
d3.lede: Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom. Each governorate is extruded by the selected metric, so the terrain you are looking at is the data itself. Simplified national geometry — a visualisation, not a survey product.
orb.lede: A simplified circular-orbit propagator running in your browser, initialised with the nominal sun-synchronous parameters of the Transporter-6 deployment. It is a teaching model: it does not read a TLE, it is not connected to a ground station, and the numbers below are computed here, not received from space.
orb.warn: Simulated values. These are outputs of a circular two-body model with a fixed inclination, not measurements. Real pass prediction requires current orbital elements and a proper propagator.
an.lede: Ask a question about the dataset. The analyst answers in a fixed structure — what it looked at, what it found, how confident it is, what it suggests next, and which kind of data the answer rests on. It runs entirely inside this page over the reference dataset: there is no external model, no API key and no network call.
an.guard: Guardrail active: the analyst refuses questions it has no data for, and labels the data type of every answer.
ag.lede: The analyst answers one question. The agent runs the whole route: collect, validate, analyse, decide, recommend, report — stopping at two real decision points where the branch actually depends on the data.
st.h: A Greener Kuwait Starts From Above
v35.lede: This is an independent platform. It has no endorsement, mandate or affiliation. What it does have is a clear line of sight to the kinds of national goals that satellite-derived environmental intelligence could serve.
v35.note: No claim of official endorsement is made or implied. Kuwait's national development programme is referred to here only as public context.
gr.h: What this system will not do
gr.lede: An environmental agent that can be wrong in public needs stated limits. These are enforced in the code on this page, not just written down.
tm.lede: Five roles, five defensible contributions. Each card states what that member can be asked about during judging.
tm.note: Names are placeholders — replace the five entries in the TEAM array near the top of this page's script with your own. Roles and contributions are already written to match the sections above.
src.lede: This table is the audit trail. If a statement about KuwaitSat-1 appears anywhere on this page, it appears here with its source. Anything not in this table is simulated, modelled or conceptual, and is badged as such where it appears.
src.provp: Every dataset and layer the platform uses, and which class it belongs to. If a layer is not in this register, it is not used.
src.not: What this platform does not claim
fin.lab: The whole point, in one sentence
fin.q: “We look at Kuwait from space — so we can better understand, plan, and monitor Kuwait on the ground.”
fin.note: This is a decision-support platform. It is not an official government planning system, it carries no endorsement, and nothing in it should be acted on without review by the competent authorities.
ft.tag: From Space to a Greener Kuwait — satellite-derived environmental decision support.

ft.l2: No live telemetry. No official planning authority.
ft.l3: Satellite photographs remain the property of their publishers.
